keyVerseText: The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly. rash: Heb. hasty plainly: or, elegantly
rootMeaning: The Hebrew adjective עִלֵּג (ʻillêg) originates from an unused root that means to stutter, emphasizing a speech impediment characterized by inarticulate or broken speech. This root sense highlights not merely difficulty in speaking but a specific form of verbal hesitation or faltering. Unlike the broader English term 'stammerer,' the original Hebrew conveys a vivid picture of disrupted communication, which can symbolize deeper barriers to clear expression or understanding.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in the Hebrew Scriptures, specifically in Isaiah 32:4, where it is translated as 'of the stammerers.' Its singular occurrence and consistent translation reflect a precise and focused usage referring to those who speak with difficulty or inarticulately. The phrase לְשׁוֺן עִלְּנִים (tongue of the stammerers) in Isaiah conveys a group characterized by this speech pattern, underscoring the contrast between unclear and clear communication.
theologicalSignificance: The concept of עִלֵּג as a stammerer reminds believers of the human limitations in expressing divine truth and knowledge. It points to the transformative power of God to bring clarity and understanding where once there was confusion or hesitation. In the Christian faith, this can be seen as a metaphor for spiritual growth—moving from faltering speech to confident proclamation of God's word. It also encourages humility, recognizing that even the most hesitant voices can be used by God to reveal wisdom and truth.
keyVerseReflection: Isaiah 32:4 states, 'The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.' Here, the word עִלֵּג highlights a transition from unclear or hesitant speech to clear and elegant expression. This transformation signifies the blessing of understanding and the ability to communicate wisdom effectively, illustrating God's work in enabling even those who once struggled to articulate truth to now speak with confidence and clarity.
